newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end mixed, market consolidates.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end mixed, market consolidates.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished mixed Wednesday in a market which consolidated recent gains rather than benefitting in full from a surge in U.S. Treasuries.
Low activity added to the failure of the market to keep pace with U.S. Treasuries, but a sensation that profit-taking could be about to set in also held the market back, said traders.
The 30-year U.S. Treasury yield fell six basis points to 6.33 percent.
"It is a very difficult market right now," said a trader at a local brokerage house, alluding to its high levels.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 1/8 at 95-1/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 edged up $0.09 to 118.80.
While Argentina's Discount and FRB Brady bonds suffered, Par bonds rose 1/8 to 75-3/8. There was talk of the Par bond benefitting from switching out of Discount bonds, said traders.
Another trader said activity was likely to pick up in coming sessions with the release of the much awaited U.S. jobless report Friday.
In the money markets, the three-month peso BAIBOR, the Buenos Aires interbank offered rate, was flat at 7.0625 percent.
